steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rapid boil. Cook egg noodles at a boil until tender yet firm to the bite, 7 to 9 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat butter and cream in a small saucepan over low heat until butter melted. Stir in cheese, parsley, salt, and pepper; keep warm over low heat.
Drain egg noodles; toss with sauce to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Noodles Alfredo
raw_recipe.description: Butter, cream, Parmesan and parsley combine almost effortlessly to make a rich and flavorful sauce to toss with tender egg noodles.
raw_recipe.name: Noodles Alfredo

review.reviewBody: The recipe as is deserves about 3.5 stars, it is a bit bland. However, I made some changes that made it excellent! We like extra sauce, so this is what I did. I doubled the heavy cream but kept the butter amount the same. I then added in a few tablespoons of cream cheese. I used 3/4 cup of grated Romano cheese and a large handful of shredded mozzarella to make it creamier. I also added in 2 teaspoons of garlic powder for some additional flavor. I then let that sit on the warmer on my stove and sauteed some chicken in garlic and butter. I served the sauce over fettucine noodles and put the chicken on top of it. Garlic bread on the side completed a fantastic meal!!

I first made this a month ago, and the only things I changed were to use twice the amount of heavy whipping cream while keeping the butter amount the same, adding in a teaspoon of garlic powder, and a handful of mozzarella cheese. Also, since shredded parmesan doesn't always melt nicely and smooth, once it's hot and the mozzarella has melted, I pour it into my BlendTec blender and give it a few pulses. This smooths it out very nicely. Be careful to hold the lid on with a dish towel covering your hand as you do not want to accidentally burn yourself.

It is excellent. My kids loved it. I pair it with homemade breadsticks, and we all love dipping the breadsticks into the sauce. 

We are having it again tonight. Yum! Thank you for the recipe, WILDFLOWER12!

After reading the reviews I was afraid adding mozzarella may make the sauce a little stringy, so here is what I did. I melted the 1/2 cup butter in a large sauce pan and sauted 1 clove of finely minced garlic, about 30 seconds. I added 8 ounces of softened cream cheese, and only 3/4 cup grated parmesan cheese; sprinkled in some white pepper to taste and the parsley (I didn't add any salt). Stirred that constantly until the cheeses were melted and butter was fully incorporated (if the sauce isn’t hot enough it may seem grainy or separated but keep heating and stirring and it will come together.) I then added 3/4 cup of milk (didn’t have any cream) and stirred until the sauce came to a simmer and started to bubble around the sides of the pan. I put the 8 ounces of hot, cooked and drained noodles into a serving bowl and added the sauce, tossing to coat. This turned out smooth and creamy, and absolutely delicious! This sauce thickens as it cools, so serve immediately. If the sauce does thicken, or you like your sauce thinner; just stir in a little additional milk. You can add hot cooked chicken, shrimp or vegetables, along with the noodles. Also makes a great sauce for chicken or vegetable lasagna or white pizza.

The other night my husband requested something with egg noodles and broccoli. I had no idea what to make, so I started looking and stumbled across this recipe. I had to improvise a bit as I didn't have grated parmesan, so I just used grated marble cheese instead. I added 3 grated garlic cloves to the butter (we like a lot of garlic) and cooked for about 30 seconds before adding in the rest of the ingredients. I steamed some broccoli and added some shrimp to the sauce - tossed everything together and it was a complete hit! Thank you so much for sharing this easy and delicious recipe!!

Good recipe but I also had a problem with my cheese melting. I added 4 oz of cream cheese and kept the sauce on low until it melted and that seemed to help some. I also addedd 1/2 tsp of minced garlic.

Probably the best homemade alfredo sauce I've made so far. I used fettucine pasta and also made some modifications to the recipe. I added a little bit of minced garlic as well as garlic salt for flavor. I also added 4 oz of cream cheese and a couple tbsp of chicken broth as well. When it was almost done, as I was stirring, I noticed that it was a little too "soup-y" so I added a little more heavy whipping cream. And I didn't have any parsley, so I left that out. It came out rich and delicious. I ate more than I could handle. I was a little grossed out that some of the butter leaked all the way down to the bottom of the bowl, so maybe next time I'll decrease the amount of butter I put in this sauce. Thanks for the recipe!
Letting the cream and butter simmer at a low heat will make it creamier and take out the grittiness out of the cheese. I also add 2 tbs of cream cheese during the simmer to add creaminess.

This is wonderful! I did make some changes mentioned by another review, I doubled the cream and added romano, garlic and a handful of mozzarella. I also added some spinach to the sauce at the end. I served it over egg noddles with slices of chicken breast.

As is this recipe is a bit heavy and bland. I used less than half the butter and added a large clove of freshly minced garlic to to the butter and soften until I could smell the garlic odor coming off before adding the cream. I was very generous with the fresh ground black pepper. But now we have a classic Alfredo sauce. :) Add roasted chicken and broccoli for a fast main dish, or one of my favorites is to add smoked salmon.

Delicious and very easy. I have added this into the regular routine and make it every 2-3 weeks. I have used 2% milk, half and half and heavy cream, (and mixed them) depending on what I had on hand, and all worked fine - heavy cream was just more smooth. I have also added garlic and enjoyed the results.

Good recipe. I followed suggestions of other reviewers and added 3T lite cream cheese, 1cup part skim mozzarella cheese, garlic powder and substituted 1 cup half & half for heavy cream. That brought it up to 5 stars! Everyone loved it! Thanks for a great recipe Wildflower.
The ultimate comfort food! This is perfect and easy when you're craving alfredo!
Very nice sauce ! I added pecorino romano cheese along with the parmesan then added basil !
It was great and easy

So quick and easy! I added a few peas to brighten it up! I'm wondering how other cheeses or vegetables might work! With the simplicity of butter, cream and cheese as a base, you could add any veggie or meat and it would be great!
Soooo easy, and our family loves it!!
This is an amazing recipe, instead of adding parsley I added chicken stock.
I should have read the reviews before I made it. It was so bland. I will remake it again but will do it with suggestions from other reviewers.

Perfect, just what I was looking for. I only made a couple changes. I didn't want to use up all my Parmesan cheese so I used half that the the rest with regular american cheese. Turned out perfect. Thanks for the great recipe.
My family loved it! Quick, easy and tasty
